children: U.S. Consumer Price Index is expected to rise 3.4% year-over-year in August, the same pace seen in July. On a monthly basis, headline CPI is expected to grow at a rate of 0.4%, accelerating from the 0.1% increase recorded in
The Bureau of Labor Statistics is scheduled to release its August CPI report on Friday, September 11, at 8:30 AM ET.

Core CPI, which excludes volatile energy and food prices, is expected to rise 2.4% from the prior year (decelerating from the 2.5% growth seen in July) and 0.2% from a month ago (in line with the pace recorded in July).

"The first inflation data that we received this week was largely in line with expectations and shouldn't have too much impact on the market," said Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer for Northlight Asset Management, citing the
"However, tomorrow's inflation data is highly anticipated as the CPI could have a big impact on a divided Federal Reserve," said Zaccarelli.

"We are in a seasonally weak period of a midterm election year, which are two reasons why markets would struggle at this point (e.g. September is the weakest month on average and markets are typically soft leading up to an election)," he said.

Meanwhile, David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation, said, "Backward-looking CPI reports have become less important than real-time moves in oil prices. CPI forecasts are rising along with crude and diesel, so it’s a small comfort if the actual numbers are below consensus."
the CPI to rise again in August, according to Chris Lau, Seeking Alpha analyst and Investing Group Leader.

"Rising diesel prices added to transportation costs. That might raise the index for food at home by between 0.1% and 0.5%, compared to 0.1% in July," said Lau. "The index for shelter consistently increased at a median of 0.1% - 0.3% this year."

"The August CPI report has a good chance of revealing that inflationary pressures worsened. The positive impact of tariff refunds ended," said Lau. "The ongoing Iran conflict continued in August, pushing energy prices higher."

Apollo Global Management chief economist Torsten Slok now expects the Federal Open Market Committee to raise interest rates at its mid-September meeting, citing mounting evidence that price pressures are reaccelerating rather than fading.

The probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the September FOMC meeting now stands at 71.6% (49.4% a week ago), compared with 28.4% odds (50.6% a week ago) of maintaining the target rate at 3.50% to 3.75%, according to the CME Fed Watch tool.

"The September Fed decision looked finely balanced at the turn of the month. September's surge in energy prices will likely tip the balance towards a hike when the Fed meets next week. A big surprise from the August CPI report's release tomorrow or a last-minute deal with Iran could still influence the decision," said Bill Adams, chief U.S. economist at Fifth Third Commercial Bank.

title: Investors price in hot August CPI reading; big surprise could sway upcoming FOMC decision
